newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Car bomb targets Bulgarian bank liquidator. [CORRECTED 15:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Car bomb targets Bulgarian bank liquidator. [CORRECTED 15:15 GMT]

text.p: Unknown assailants launched a car bomb attack on Thursday against a senior official who is chief liquidator of a Bulgarian bank and a member of the country's Central Electoral Committee, Bulgarian national radio reported.
The official, Haralambi Anchev, was not hurt in the blast from the home-made bomb, which damaged buildings and cars in central Sofia. The radio described it as a "terrorist act".
(Corrects to make clear Bulgarian radio described attack as "terrorist", not Anchev) The Bulgarian Agricultural and Industrial Bank was set up by businessmen close to the ruling Socialists.
The Sofia City Court cancelled its registration earlier this year, citing legal inconsistencies in the list of shareholders and appointed liquidators to close it down.
Anchev also holds a senior position on Bulgaria's Central Electoral Committee, which is preparing for the second round of presidential elections on Sunday.
Bomb attacks have become common in Bulgaria, where the crime rate has soared since the collapse of the communism in 1989.
